chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Sulami, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

Some of the Khawarij asked me about this verse: 'Of sheep, two; and of goats, two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females? Or what is in the wombs of the two females? Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of camels, two; and of cows, two.' What is that which Allah has permitted from that, and what is that which He has prohibited? But I did not have anything (to answer with).

So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was a pilgrim, and I informed him of what had happened. He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted in the sacrificial offering in Mina the domestic sheep and the domestic goat, and prohibited that one sacrifice the mountain (wild) ones.'

And as for His words 'And of camels, two; and of cows, two', indeed Allah, Blessed and High, permitted in the sacrificial offering the Iraab camel, and prohibited the Bukhaty in it; and permitted the domestic cow that one sacrifice with it, and prohibited the mountain (wild) one.
So I returned to the man and informed him with this answer. He said: 'This is something which the camels carried from Al-Hijaaz.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between domestic and wild animals for Hajj sacrifices according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic verse 6:143-143 refers to the specific characteristics of sacrificial animals in Mina, distinguishing between domesticated ('Ahlīyah') and wild/mountainous ('Jabaliyah') varieties of sheep, goats, camels, and cattle. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly approach to interpreting general Quranic verses through specific Prophetic traditions, resolving the ambiguity of 'which two?' by linking it to the practical requirements of the Udhiyah sacrifice. The context underscores the importance of animal suitability for ritual sacrifice, a key topic in Fiqh al-Udhiyah.
